title: Justin Bieber
wiki_lead:
Justin Drew Bieber ( BEE-bər; born March 1, 1994) is a Canadian singer. An influential figure in popular music, Bieber is known for his image reinventions and multi-genre performances. With estimated sales of over 150 million records, he is one of the best-selling music artists of all time.
Bieber rose to fame in the late 2000s after being discovered by American talent manager Scooter Braun, who signed him to Raymond Braun Media Group (RBMG). Bieber subsequently released his debut extended play (EP), My World (2009), which earned him international recognition and established him as a teen idol. His debut studio album, My World 2.0 (2010), topped the US Billboard 200, making him the youngest solo male to do so in 47 years. Its lead single, "Baby", became one of the best-selling singles in the United States. His second album, Under the Mistletoe (2011), became the first Christmas album by a male artist to debut on top of the chart. With his third studio album, Believe (2012), and its acoustic re-release (2013), Bieber became the first artist to have five US number-one albums by the age of eighteen.
Bieber's EDM-infused single "Where Are Ü Now" set the tone for his fourth studio album, Purpose (2015). It yielded three US Billboard Hot 100 number-one singles: "Love Yourself", "Sorry", and "What Do You Mean?". The songs also occupied the top three of the UK singles chart, which Bieber was the first artist in history to achieve. In 2017, he featured on the US number-one singles "I'm the One" and "Despacito"; the latter tied the then-record for the most weeks at number one in history. His following two studio albums, Changes (2020) and Justice (2021), debuted at number one, making Bieber the youngest solo act to have eight US number-one albums. He released two US number-one singles in 2021, "Peaches" and "Stay". After a brief hiatus, he released his seventh and eighth studio albums, Swag and Swag II, in 2025.
Bieber's accolades include 2 Grammy Awards, 1 Latin Grammy Award, 8 Juno Awards, 2 Brit Awards, 26 Billboard Music Awards, 19 American Music Awards, 6 MTV Video Music Awards and a record 22 MTV Europe Music Awards. Time named him one of the 100 most influential people in 2011, and Forbes listed him among the top 10 most powerful celebrities from 2011 to 2013. In 2024, Billboard ranked him the eighth greatest pop star of the 21st century. Outside of music, Bieber has co-founded the clean water technology company Generosity, and launched the clothing lines Drew House and Skylrk. He was the recipient of the Queen Elizabeth II Diamond Jubilee Medal in 2012.

He was the recipient of the Queen Elizabeth II Diamond Jubilee Medal in 2012.


Life and career


Early life
Justin Drew Bieber was born on March 1, 1994, in London, Ontario, and was raised in Stratford. His parents, Jeremy Bieber and Pattie Mallette, separated soon after his birth. Mallette raised Bieber as a single mother in low-income housing. Mallette's mother Diane and stepfather Bruce helped her raise Bieber, who has maintained contact with his father. Bieber has French, Irish, English, and German ancestry. Through his father, Bieber has two younger half-sisters and a younger half-brother. He also has a stepsister, who is the daughter of his stepmother. Growing up, Bieber learned to play the drums and piano; his mother bought his first drum set when he was four and his first guitar when he was six. He performed in church benefits at age eight.
Bieber attended two French-language immersion elementary schools in Stratford: Jeanne Sauvé Catholic School and Bedford Public School. In grades 7 and 8, he attended Stratford Northwestern Secondary School. He then attended St. Michael Catholic Secondary School, graduating in 2012 with a 4.0 GPA.


2007–2009: Career beginnings and My World
In early 2007, aged 12, Bieber performed a cover of Ne-Yo's "So Sick" for a local singing competition in Stratford, in which he placed in the top three. Mallette posted a video of the performance on YouTube for their family and friends to see. She continued to upload videos of Bieber singing covers of various R&B songs, and Bieber's popularity on the site grew. In the same year, Bieber busked in front of the Avon Theatre.
While searching for videos of a different singer, Scooter Braun, a former marketing executive of So So Def Recordings, clicked on one of Bieber's 2007 YouTube videos by accident, where he was covering "So Sick". Impressed, Braun tracked down Bieber's school, the theatre Bieber was performing at, and finally his mother Mallette, who was initially reluctant because of Braun's Judaism; she wanted him to sign with "a Christian man, a Christian label". However, church elders convinced her to let Bieber go with Braun. At age 13, Bieber went to Atlanta, Georgia, with Braun to record demo tapes. Bieber began singing for Usher one week later. Bieber soon signed with Raymond Braun Media Group (RBMG), a joint venture between Braun and Usher. Singer Justin Timberlake was also in the running to sign Bieber but lost the bidding war to Usher.
Usher then sought assistance in finding a label home for the artist from then-manager Chris Hicks, who helped engineer an audition with his contact L.A. Reid of the Island Def Jam Music Group. Reid signed Bieber to Island Records in October 2008 (resulting in a joint venture between RBMG and Island Records) and appointed Hicks as executive vice-president of Def Jam, where he could manage Bieber's career at the label. Bieber then moved to Atlanta with his mother to pursue further work with Braun and Usher. Braun became Bieber's manager in 2008.

Bieber's first single, "One Time", was released to radio while he was still recording his debut album. The song reached number 12 on the Canadian Hot 100 during its first week of release in July 2009, and peaked at number 17 on the US Billboard Hot 100 chart. The song was certified platinum in Canada and the US and gold in Australia and New Zealand. His first release, an extended play (EP) titled My World, was released on November 17, 2009. The EP's second single, "One Less Lonely Girl", charted within the top 20 of the Billboard Hot 100. It also peaked within the top 20 in Canada. 
My World was eventually certified platinum in the US and double platinum in both Canada and the United Kingdom. To promote the EP, Bieber performed on several live shows such as MTVU's VMA Tour, YTV's The Next Star, and Today's Toyota Concert Series. He also appeared on It's On with Alexa Chung, The Ellen DeGeneres Show, and The Wendy Williams Show. Bieber guest starred in an episode of True Jackson, VP in late 2009. He performed Ron Miller and Bryan Wells's "Someday at Christmas" for US president Barack Obama and First Lady Michelle Obama at the White House for Christmas in Washington, which aired on December 20, 2009.


2010–2011: My World 2.0, Never Say Never, and Under the Mistletoe

Bieber was a presenter at the 52nd Annual Grammy Awards on January 31, 2010. He was invited to be a vocalist for the remake of the charity single "We Are the World" for its 25th anniversary to benefit Haiti after the 2010 earthquake. Bieber sings the opening line, which was sung by Lionel Richie in the original version. In January 2010, "Baby" featuring Ludacris was released as the lead single to his debut album, My World 2.0. The song charted at number five on the Billboard Hot 100, number three on the Canadian Hot 100, and in the top 10 in several international markets. The album received generally favourable reviews. It debuted at number one on the US Billboard 200, making Bieber the youngest solo male act to top the chart since Stevie Wonder in 1963. My World 2.0 also debuted at number one in Australia, Canada, Ireland, and New Zealand.
My World 2.0's following singles included "Eenie Meenie" and a remix of "Somebody to Love" featuring Usher. On June 23, Bieber went on his first official headlining tour, the My World Tour, to promote My World and My World 2.0. In May 2010, Bieber featured in rapper Soulja Boy's song "Rich Girl". In July, his video for "Baby" surpassed Lady Gaga's "Bad Romance" (2009) as the most viewed, and most disliked, YouTube video at the time. 

Bieber guest-starred in the season premiere of the CBS American crime drama CSI: Crime Scene Investigation, which aired on September 23, 2010. He played a troubled teenager with an "explosive" brother. Bieber was in a subsequent episode of the series, which aired on February 17, 2011, in which his character is killed. Bieber performed a medley of his singles "U Smile", "Baby", and "Somebody to Love", and briefly played the drums, at the 2010 MTV Video Music Awards on September 12, 2010. Bieber released My Worlds Acoustic on November 26, 2010, in the United States. The album featured acoustic versions of songs from his previous albums, and accompanied the release of a new song titled "Pray". In October 2010, Bieber released his first book, Justin Bieber: First Step 2 Forever: My Story, an autobiography with text from Bieber and photographs from Robert Caplin.
A 3-D part-biopic, part-concert film starring Bieber entitled Justin Bieber: Never Say Never, was released on February 11, 2011, directed by Jon M. Chu. The film was a box office success, while critics gave it mixed reviews. Never Say Never reportedly exceeded industry expectations and became one of the highest debuts for a music-documentary. Never Say Never grossed a total of $99 million worldwide, becoming the highest-grossing concert or performance film at the global box office. The film is accompanied by his second remix album, Never Say Never: The Remixes, released on February 14, 2011, and features remixes of songs from his debut album, with guest appearances from Miley Cyrus, Chris Brown, and Kanye West, among others. In 2011, Time named Bieber one of the 100 most influential people on their annual list. Also in June, Bieber was ranked number two on Forbes' list of Best-Paid Celebrities under 30.
On November 1, 2011, Bieber released the Christmas album Under the Mistletoe, his second studio album. It became the first Christmas album by a male artist to debut atop the Billboard 200, and sold 210,000 copies in its first week. Billboard named it one of the most successful holiday albums in the US in 2021. The first single from the album, "Mistletoe", peaked at number one on the US Billboard Holiday 100 and Holiday Digital Songs charts. Billboard listed the album and its singles among the greatest holiday albums and songs of all time, respectively.


2012–2014: Believe, Journals, and other appearances

In late 2011, Bieber began recording his third studio album, titled Believe. The following week, Bieber appeared on The Ellen DeGeneres Show to announce that the first single would be titled "Boyfriend", which was released on March 26, 2012. The song debuted at number two on the Billboard Hot 100, selling a total of 521,000 digital units, the second-highest-ever debut digital sales week. "Boyfriend" debuted atop the Canadian Hot 100—his first number-one on the chart. The second single from Believe, "As Long as You Love Me" featuring rapper Big Sean, was released in June 2012. It peaked at number six on the Billboard Hot 100.
Island Records released Believe on June 19, 2012. The album marked a musical departure from the teen pop sound of his previous releases, and incorporated elements of dance-pop and R&B genres. Believe debuted at number one on the Billboard 200, becoming his fourth number-one album. The album sold 57,000 copies in its first week in Canada, debuting atop the Canadian Albums Chart. In October 2012, the third single from Believe, "Beauty and a Beat" featuring Nicki Minaj, was released. The music video held the record for the most video views in 24 hours when it was released, with 10.6 million views.

The Believe Tour, which promoted Believe, began in September 2012. On January 29, 2013, Bieber released an acoustic album titled Believe Acoustic. The album debuted at number one on the Billboard 200, making Bieber the first artist in history
